report.source_text: Neurological examination revealed reduced consciousness (Glasgow Coma Scale score of 12: E4V2M6), expressive aphasia, bilateral partial ptosis with ophthalmoplegia, bilateral cerebellar signs including dysdiadochokinesia, and past-pointing with mild truncal ataxia. He had normal tone and hyperreflexia in both knee and ankle jerks. Power was 5 (based on Medical Research Council grading) in both upper and lower limbs. His right eye was held in an adducted, downward gaze, whereas his left eye held a central, downward gaze, suggesting cranial nerves III and IV palsy, respectively.

report.source_text: The patient was promptly initiated on immunotherapy with intravenous (IV) methylprednisolone 1000 mg daily for 5 days and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) 2 g/kg over two days. He also received one dose of IV tocilizumab 8 mg/kg 12 hours from hospital presentation. Normothermia at 35°C to 36°C was maintained for six days. Serum sodium levels were kept minimally at 140 mmol/L for neuroprotection. He received a five-day course of IV remdesivir to treat SARS-CoV-2. Other concurrent antimicrobials included empirical IV ceftriaxone, azithromycin, acyclovir, and oseltamivir, until respective viral and bacterial studies returned negative.

report.source_text: After eight days, he demonstrated good response to treatment; Glasgow Coma Scale improved to 15, ophthalmoplegia and ataxia improved, and mRS score reduced to 2. He was discharged home after 16 days with residual deficits including mild ophthalmoplegia, upper limb dysmetria with intention tremor, mild aphasia, and dysarthria. At discharge, mRS score was 1. Two weeks later, mRS score improved to 0, indicating neurological function recovery.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 11-year-old boy presented with acute neurological symptoms including reduced consciousness, expressive aphasia, ophthalmoplegia, and cerebellar signs, following a SARS-CoV-2 infection. Neurological examination confirmed these deficits (E001). Brain MRI showed characteristic swelling and signal changes in bilateral thalami, midbrain, pons, cerebellar hemispheres, and periventricular white matter, correlating with ANEC (E002). CSF analysis revealed elevated red cells and protein but no pleocytosis, and negative infectious and autoimmune panels (E003, E004). He was treated with immunotherapy (IV methylprednisolone, IVIG, tocilizumab), IV remdesivir, and empirical antimicrobials (E007). He showed good response to treatment, with GCS improving to 15, and resolution of ophthalmoplegia and ataxia. He was discharged after 16 days with residual deficits that fully resolved within two weeks, achieving an mRS score of 0 (E008).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with acute neurological symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Neurological examination revealed reduced consciousness (GCS 12), expressive aphasia, bilateral partial ptosis with ophthalmoplegia, bilateral cerebellar signs, hyperreflexia, and specific gaze deviations suggesting CN III and IV palsy.
Brain MRI showed swelling and signal changes involving bilateral thalami, midbrain, pons, cerebellar hemispheres, and periventricular white matter, correlating with a diagnosis of ANEC.
CSF analysis showed elevated red cell count (25 cells/uL) and protein (1.02 g/L), normal opening pressure, no pleocytosis, normal glucose/lactate, and absence of oligoclonal bands.
Extensive serum and CSF autoimmune tests were negative, including anti-N-methyl-d-aspartate, anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein, anti-glutamic-acid-decarboxylase, and anti-GQ1b-ganglioside IgG.
CSF meningoencephalitis infectious panel, including SARS-CoV-2 PCR, returned negative.
Treatment included IV methylprednisolone, IVIG, IV tocilizumab, IV remdesivir, and empirical antimicrobials.
Patient demonstrated good response to treatment, with GCS improving to 15, improved ophthalmoplegia and ataxia, and full neurological recovery (mRS score 0) within two weeks post-discharge.
